about: Designed experiments from published sources other than the book, with where each came from and what the
source prints for it. Factorial opens each by name: https://factori.al/?example=<name>.
sources: one citation per source, by key; read: when and from what the numbers were taken.
examples: as web/book-examples.json holds the book's (design, model, runs in the order the source lists them,
settings in coded units and the result last), with source, the key of its citation, and where, the section,
figures, tables and pages its runs are printed on. published: the results the source prints, each group with
where it is printed; numbers are text as printed, so the decimals printed set how closely they are checked.
library_examples: published examples the app cannot open (a categorical factor at three levels), as rows
for the library to fit with model.
tests/web/api/test_published_examples.py checks every published number, and that every example says where it came from.

ullmann-doe-2012.title: Design of Experiments
ullmann-doe-2012.publisher: Wiley-VCH Verlag GmbH & Co. KGaA, Weinheim
ullmann-doe-2012.cite: Soravia and Orth (2012), "Design of Experiments", Ullmann's Encyclopedia of Industrial Chemistry
ullmann-doe-2012.read: 2026-10-13, from the article's PDF (article e08_e01), every number checked against the library

examples.name: ullmann-catalyst-temperature
examples.title: Yield against catalyst A and temperature B, with a centre run
examples.where: Section 3.2, Figure 5 (p. 174); the centre run, pp. 175 to 176 and Table 4 (p. 187)
examples.note: A is the quantity of catalyst and B the reaction temperature in a stirred tank.

fitted.where: Table 4 (p. 187), in the order of the runs

residuals.where: Table 4 (p. 187), the observed less the fitted value

left_out_predictions.where: Table 5 (p. 188): each run predicted by the model fitted without it

examples.name: ullmann-agitator
examples.title: Yield against catalyst A, temperature B and agitator type C
examples.note: C, the agitator type, is categorical: the current one or a new one. With every interaction in the model, no degrees of freedom are left, as in the article, which works with the effects alone.

effects.where: Section 3.3, Figure 9 (p. 178) and the summary of effects (p. 179)

examples.name: ullmann-agitator-half-fraction
examples.title: Half fraction of the agitator experiment: catalyst A, temperature B, agitator type C
examples.note: Four of the eight runs of the full experiment, chosen with C = A·B: the effect of C cannot be told apart from the interaction of A and B.

expressions.where: Figure 10 (p. 180): the main effect of C, which is also the interaction of A and B

library_examples.name: ullmann-three-level-categorical
library_examples.title: One categorical factor at three instances, coded by two dummy variables
library_examples.note: The article codes instance i1 as (p1, p2) = (1, 0), i2 as (0, 1) and i3 as (-1, -1): sum-to-zero coding.

coefficients.where: Section 7.2 (p. 198): c0, c1 and c2, and c3 = -c1 - c2 for the third instance
